A section of the 20 Department of Transportation (DOT) representation also deals with the Philadelphia area. Using statistics for the Philadelphia Urbanized Area, as defined by the Bureau 21 of Census, and the Philadelphia SMSA, the following points were made:
(1) From 1960 to 1970 manufacturing and trade employment in the Philadelphia SMSA increased by 9.6 percent, whereas manufacturing and trade employment in the existing commercial zone decreased during the same period by 10.0 percent;
(2) In 1960, 78.9 percent of Philadelphia SMSA manufacturing and trade employment was concentrated within present commercial zone limits. In 1970, this figure had dropped to 64.7 percent.
(3) In 1970, approximately 70.8 percent of SMSA manufacturing and trade firms were located within the commercial zone. Figures for 1960 in this category are not available.
(4) Of the 249 industrial parks in the Philadelphia SMSA, only 67, or 26.9 percent, are in the present commercial zone.

The DOT representation at the interim stage of this proceeding included a general statement of its position with supporting arguments, verified statements by two persons having a background in transportation research and analysis, and the results of a study of the Atlanta and Boston commercial zones conducted by a private transportation research and consulting firm. DOT's representation is summarized in the Interim Report, Commercial Zones, 124 M.C.C. at 148-152.

lt;sup>21</sup>Bureau of Census Urbanized Areas include a central city with a population of 50,000 or more and a surrounding area (Urban Fringe) determined according to population density. The Urban Fringe consists of that territory having at least 1,000 inhabitants per square mile and separated by no more than 1.5 miles from the main body of the Urban Area.
The Philadelphia SMSA consists of Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia Counties in Pennsylvania and Burlington, Camden, and Gloucester Counties in New Jersey.
